subject: Biology
title: Breathing and Exchange of Gases
summary: Breathing (ventilation) mein atmospheric air andar lete hain aur CO₂-rich hawa bahar chhodte hain. Respiration mein iske baad alveoli mein gas exchange, blood se gas transport, tissues mein exchange aur cells mein O₂ ka use aata hai.

Inspiration active process hai — diaphragm aur external intercostal muscles contract karke thoracic volume badhaate hain, pressure atmosphere se kam hota hai aur hawa andar aati hai. Normal expiration passive hai.
Gas exchange simple diffusion se hota hai — partial pressure gradient, solubility aur membrane ki motai par depend karta hai. CO₂ ki solubility O₂ se 20–25 guna zyada hai.

Lagbhag 97% O₂ haemoglobin se (oxyhaemoglobin) aur 3% plasma mein ghul kar jaata hai. CO₂ ka 20–25% carbamino-haemoglobin, ~70% bicarbonate aur ~7% plasma mein dissolved. Breathing ka rhythm medulla ka respiratory rhythm centre banata hai.

formulas.name: Respiratory volumes
formulas.mistake: RV kabhi bahar nahi nikalta — isliye spirometer RV aur TLC seedha nahi naap sakta.

formulas.name: Inspiratory capacity
formulas.when: Normal expiration ke baad kitni hawa andar ja sakti hai.

formulas.name: Expiratory capacity
formulas.when: Normal inspiration ke baad kitni hawa bahar nikal sakti hai.

formulas.name: Functional residual capacity
formulas.when: Normal expiration ke baad lungs mein bachi hawa.

formulas.name: Vital capacity
formulas.when: Forced inspiration ke baad max kitni hawa nikal sakti hai.

formulas.name: Total lung capacity
formulas.formula: TLC = RV + ERV + TV + IRV = VC + RV
formulas.when: Forced inspiration ke baad lungs mein total hawa.

formulas.name: Pulmonary ventilation
formulas.formula: minute volume = TV × breathing rate ≈ 500 × 12–16 = 6000–8000 mL/min
formulas.note: Healthy adult 12–16 baar per minute saans leta hai.

formulas.name: Partial pressures (mm Hg)
formulas.formula: pO₂ / pCO₂:  atmosphere 159 / 0.3;  alveoli 104 / 40;  deoxygenated blood 40 / 45;  oxygenated blood 95 / 40;  tissues 40 / 45
formulas.note: Gas hamesha zyada partial pressure se kam ki taraf jaati hai.

formulas.name: Diffusion membrane
formulas.formula: alveolar squamous epithelium + basement substance + capillary endothelium (total < 1 mm)

formulas.name: Oxygen transport
formulas.formula: 97% Hb (oxyhaemoglobin, har Hb max 4 O₂);  3% plasma;  100 mL oxygenated blood tissues ko ~5 mL O₂ deta hai

formulas.name: Oxygen dissociation curve
formulas.formula: % saturation vs pO₂ — sigmoid curve;  alveoli mein high pO₂, low pCO₂, low H⁺, low T ⇒ oxyhaemoglobin banta hai;  tissues mein ulta ⇒ O₂ chhoot-ta hai
formulas.note: Curve right shift (Bohr effect) = O₂ aasaani se chhodta hai.

formulas.name: CO₂ transport
formulas.formula: 20–25% carbamino-haemoglobin;  ~70% bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻);  ~7% dissolved in plasma;  100 mL deoxygenated blood alveoli ko ~4 mL CO₂ deta hai

formulas.name: Carbonic anhydrase reaction
formulas.formula: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + H⁺   (RBCs mein carbonic anhydrase, kuch plasma mein bhi)
formulas.note: Tissues mein reaction aage, alveoli mein peeche jaati hai.

formulas.name: Regulation of respiration
formulas.formula: respiratory rhythm centre (medulla);  pneumotaxic centre (pons) — inspiration ki duration kam karke rate badhata hai;  chemosensitive area (medulla) — CO₂ aur H⁺ ke prati;  aortic arch aur carotid artery receptors
formulas.note: O₂ ka role rhythm mein bahut kam hai; CO₂/H⁺ main signal hain.

examples.problem: Cardiac output 5 L/min; har 100 mL blood ~5 mL O₂ deta hai. Tissues ko per minute kitni O₂?

examples.title: Diffusion ki direction
examples.problem: Alveoli (pO₂ 104, pCO₂ 40) aur deoxygenated blood (pO₂ 40, pCO₂ 45) ke beech gas kis taraf jaayegi?
examples.solution: O₂ alveoli se blood mein (104 → 40), CO₂ blood se alveoli mein (45 → 40). CO₂ ka gradient chhota hai par solubility 20–25 guna zyada hone se kaafi CO₂ diffuse ho jaata hai.

examples.title: Emphysema
examples.problem: Emphysema mein saans lene mein dikkat kyun?
examples.solution: Alveolar walls damage ho jaati hain, respiratory surface kam ho jaata hai — cigarette smoking iska main kaaran hai.

topics.title: Respiratory organs in animals
topics.explain: Lower invertebrates (sponges, coelenterates, flatworms) — body surface se simple diffusion. Earthworm — moist cuticle. Insects — tracheal tubes. Aquatic arthropods aur molluscs — gills (branchial respiration). Fish — gills. Amphibians — skin (cutaneous) aur lungs. Reptiles, birds, mammals — lungs (pulmonary respiration).

topics.title: Human respiratory system
topics.explain: External nostrils → nasal chamber → pharynx → larynx (sound box; epiglottis khana andar jaane se rokta hai) → trachea → primary, secondary, tertiary bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. Trachea se initial bronchioles tak incomplete cartilaginous rings support dete hain. Lungs double-layered pleura se dhake; pleural fluid friction kam karta hai. Conducting part hawa ko filter, garam aur nam karta hai; exchange part alveoli hai.

topics.title: Mechanism of breathing
topics.explain: Inspiration: diaphragm contract (neeche) aur external intercostal muscles contract (ribs aur sternum upar) ⇒ thoracic aur pulmonary volume badhe ⇒ intra-pulmonary pressure atmosphere se kam ⇒ hawa andar. Expiration: muscles relax ⇒ volume ghate ⇒ pressure zyada ⇒ hawa bahar. Abdominal muscles se forced breathing hoti hai.

topics.title: Exchange of gases
topics.explain: Alveoli primary site, tissues secondary. Diffusion ko partial pressure gradient, gas ki solubility aur membrane ki thickness affect karti hai. Diffusion membrane bahut patli (< 1 mm) hai.

topics.title: Transport of gases
topics.explain: Haemoglobin (RBCs ka red iron pigment) O₂ ko reversibly bind karta hai. CO₂ zyada pCO₂ par Hb se carbamino-haemoglobin banata hai aur alveoli mein chhod deta hai. RBCs mein carbonic anhydrase bicarbonate banata hai.

topics.title: Disorders of respiratory system
topics.explain: Asthma: bronchi aur bronchioles mein inflammation se wheezing aur saans lene mein dikkat. Emphysema: chronic disorder, alveolar walls damage, respiratory surface kam — main kaaran smoking. Occupational respiratory disorders: dhool (stone breaking, grinding) se lung fibrosis — protective masks pehenne chahiye.

ratta: IC = TV + IRV;  EC = TV + ERV;  FRC = ERV + RV;  VC = ERV + TV + IRV;  TLC = VC + RV.
Alveoli pO₂ 104, pCO₂ 40;  tissues pO₂ 40, pCO₂ 45.
O₂: 97% Hb, 3% plasma;  100 mL blood → 5 mL O₂.
CO₂: 20–25% carbamino, 70% HCO₃⁻, 7% plasma;  4 mL per 100 mL.
Rhythm centre medulla;  pneumotaxic centre pons.
Emphysema — smoking;  asthma — inflammation of bronchi.

Disorder match: emphysema — damaged alveolar walls, less respiratory surface;  angina — chest pain, too little O₂ to heart muscle;  glomerulonephritis — inflamed glomeruli;  tetany — rapid spasms from low Ca²⁺.
